title: Late-Return Allowance Added to Keyturn Guest Protection Plan Cover
content:
A trip that runs past its scheduled return stays covered on the same level for the late period, and an
allowance for that is added to a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election in advance where the guest's own trip
record shows they have run late before. The record read is the guest's Keyturn Trip Booking ledger, in which a
late return appears as a late return charged, and the rate plan the present trip is priced under is read from
the Keyturn Trip Booking itself.

1. Where the guest's trips carry 2 or more late returns charged over the last twelve months and the trip is
   priced on the extended stay plan or on the monthly plan, 3 late cover days are added.
2. Where the guest's trips carry exactly 1 late return charged over the last twelve months and the trip is
   priced on the extended stay plan or on the monthly plan, 2 late cover days are added.
3. In every other case, 0 late cover days are added.

## Both sides of each threshold

| Late returns charged in the last twelve months | Rate plan of the present trip | Late cover days added |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | The extended stay plan or the monthly plan | 3 |
| 2 or more | Any other rate plan | 0 |
| Exactly 1 | The extended stay plan or the monthly plan | 2 |
| Exactly 1 | Any other rate plan | 0 |
| None | Any rate plan | 0 |

## Worked on hypothetical ledgers

A guest with 3 late returns charged across their trips in the last twelve months, booking on the extended stay
plan, meets the first condition and carries 3 late cover days. The same guest booking a weekend car on another
rate plan carries none, because the allowance turns on the rate plan as well as on the count.

A guest with exactly 1 late return charged in the last twelve months, on the monthly plan, carries 2 late cover
days. A second late return charged inside the same twelve months would take the same guest to the first
condition and 3 days. A guest with no late return charged in that period carries none whatever the rate
plan.
